mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 1.2% signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.2% over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS has risen above 1.5% in the prior 3 months over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in payroll employment signals a strengthening labor market that boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts signals weakening residential demand that precedes economic slowdowns and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansions when HOUST declines over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index above its 3-month moving average indicates expanding manufacturing output that correlates with stronger corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is above its 3-month moving average over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in core consumer price index above 2.5% annualized signals accelerating inflation that prompts central bank tightening, reducing real equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation rate exceeds 2.5% over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals inflation-driven monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces real earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both rise over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in unemployment rate signals labor market improvement that boosts consumer confidence and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during high unemployment regimes when UNRATE declines over any 5-year rolling window.
